newsitem.headline: AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.

AMLC COMMENTARY: Prices for lean manufacturing beef improved

significantly in the U.S. market this week. The price lift was encouraged by stronger spot market buying and gained strength as market participants began to purchase their needs for the upcoming 4th July holiday.

U.S. fresh domestic 90CL beef gained 17 US c/lb on the spot market. Imported CIF export prices gained only a small proportion of this rise, gaining 1-7 USc/lb. Once again, the largest rises were obtained at the leaner end. These increases combined with a further ratchet down in the A$ to lift Australian exporter returns by up to 20 A.c/kg FAS.
The market for lean manufacturing beef in the U.S. should be supported in coming months by much lower offerings out of New Zealand and lower U.S. domestic cow kills.
Historically, over this time, imported beef prices generally gain some seasonal strength which should flow through to Australian cow and manufacturing steer prices.

In the Japanese market, demand for beef remains decidedly soft. Over the first third of the year, consumption was down over six percent compared with the same period in 1996 and three percent down on the volume consumed over that time in 1995.
Some press reports indicate that U.S. export offer prices to Japan are beginning to decline. This would suggest that U.S.
packers expect kills to accelerate over the next month, freeing up more product export.

Higher U.S. feed beef production and lower fed cattle prices in the U.S. will make U.S. packers more competitive in export markets, toughening competition in the north Asian region and constraining Australian export steer and bullock prices.
Although supply factors are likely to dictate market conditions in the coming weeks, demand will also play an important part.

To this end, Australian exporters will be boosted by the announcement of the seventh Korean tender for the 1997 quota year. The tender is for 8200 tonnes, over half of which is grassfed product, on which Australian packers are likely to bid very aggressively. The tender will be awarded on Friday June 27.

Turning to matters that may affect Australian markets in Eastern Europe over the longer term, the European Union beef stockpile now stands at 509,000 tonnes carcase weight as at the end of April 1997, a 100,000 tonnes increase since the beginning of the year.

A report recently released by the European Commission forecasts intervention stocks to start falling in 1998, as the emergency measures adopted in late 1996 begin to impact on production during 1998 and 1999. However, when production levels return to normal stocks are again forecast to accumulate to reach 1.5 million tonnes by 2005.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
